sentences.text:
This petition coming on for hearing this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER 1.

This petition under Article 226/227 of the Constitution of India has been filed seeking the following reliefs :-
(i) Calling the records of the respondent for acquisition of land in question.

sentences.text: (ii) Quash the notification published under Section 4 (1) annexure A-4 declaration under section 6 annexure A-5 and the notice issued under section 9 annexure A-8 in respect of land bearing khasra no. 186/1G area 0.48 acres, after holding that the land in question is not required for public purposes, i.e., it is not coming under the Doob of Baan-Sagar, Bandh, for which it is being acquired.
(iii) For directions to release the land in-question for the residential purpose of the legal heirs of late Shri Anujpal Singh and their family members.

(iii-a) For direction to quash the proceedings initiate under the Land Acquisition Act, 1984 to acquire the aforesaid land bearing khasra no.186/1G area measuring 0.48 Hect; as the same is deemed to have lapsed after coming of the new act of 2013.

(iv) Directing the respondent no. 2 to make a reference to the competent Court for deciding the just compensation in respect of the land bearing khasra no.184/2G area 3.46 acres.
(v) Issue any other Order or Orders, Writ or Writs, Direction or Directions which this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.
(vi) Cost of the petition.
2. It is submitted by counsel for the petitioner that the impugned notifications issued under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act have already been quashed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court by order dated 29.1.2007 passed in W.P.No.8593/2006.
Therefore, it is submitted that relief no. 7 (ii) has rendered infructuous in the light of the aforesaid judgment.

3. So far as relief no. 7 (iii) is concerned, it is submitted that it has also rendered infructuous in the light of the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Indore Development Authority vs.
Manoharlal and others reported in AIR 2020 SC 1496.
4.

entities.text:
Indore Development Authority vs.
Manoharlal and others reported in AIR 2020 SC 1496
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, counsel for the petitioner has pressed the prayer clause 7 (iv) by which he sought a direction to the Collector to refer the matter under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act upon acquisition of the land bearing khasra no.184/2G.
5.

So far as the relief clause, direction to the Collector to refer the matter under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act is concerned, it is fairly conceded by counsel for the petitioner that the said proceeding arises out of different land acquisition proceeding.
Thus, it is clear that this petition suffers from mis- joinder of causes of action.

6. Accordingly, this petition is permitted to be withdrawn in respect of relief sought by the petitioner seeking direction to the Collector to refer the matter under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act.
7. Accordingly, liberty is granted to the petitioner to file a fresh writ petition for the said relief.
